title: Small-win Velocity Digest (personal)
body:
Context / purpose:
This is a cramped scratchpad for a compact, 5-week micro-OKR that prioritizes small wins over a big-bang project. Goal is to build momentum for the workstream I own (developer onboarding throughput) and to test two hypotheses about friction points in the signup -> first successful call flow. Keep it tight: measure weekly, ship increments, and surface blockers early.

Micro-Objective (draft):
Increase first-day API activation and successful first-call rate by reducing onboarding friction and improving examples/docs. Focus on telemetry, one-command quickstarts, and identifying the single biggest blocker causing abandonment.

Key Results (measurable, timeboxed to 5 weeks):
- KR1: Raise successful first-call rate from 18% -> 36% (week 5). Baseline 18%.
- KR2: Reduce median time-to-first-successful-call from 48m -> 15m.
- KR3: Add 3 telemetry signals that map to abandonment causality and validate at least 1 remediation.
- KR4: Ship a one-command quickstart example and measure adoption (target 500 unique runs).

Hypotheses to test (ranking):
1) Complexity of auth/token setup is the largest drop-off (confidence: 0.7).
2) Confusing error messages (500/400s) make users stop debugging (confidence: 0.5).
3) Lack of a minimal, working SDK example causes people to bail (confidence: 0.6).

Signals / Metrics to monitor (weekly snapshot):
- funnel: signup -> token created -> example run started -> example run success
- conversion points and % drop between stages
- median time between signup and run-success
- error-type histogram for failed runs
- quickstart runs (unique ids)

(quick table, update each week)
Week 0 (baseline):  signup 12,430 | token 5,430 | run-start 2,150 | run-success 430 | success% 18% | median time 48m

Weekly check-in template (copy per week):
- Wins (small, measurable):
- Blockers (what I can't do without help):
- Data/insights (new telemetry or surprising numbers):
- Next micro-ships (what I will ship this week):
- Asks (people/api/infra/legal):

Week 1 (2025-01-13):
- Wins: Added a trimmed quickstart README and a one-file Node example. Deployed new dev token flow in staging.
- Blockers: Missing SSO service account docs; need product help.
- Data: run-start -> run-success improved to 21% in staging tests (small sample). Median time down to ~35m for staged cohort.
- Ships: landed README + example; feature-flagged improved error text for auth failures.
- Asks: @Maya to help with SSO snippet and @infra on limiting token TTL for dev tokens.

Week 2 (2025-01-20) quick notes:
- Wins: Instrumented run-failure reasons (timeout vs auth vs schema). Auth failures are 54% of failures in the sample.
- Hypothesis confirmed: auth is biggest lever.
- Action: prioritize streamlined token creation + copy improvements.

Retrospective (mid-run):
- What worked: small, visible pushes kept momentum. Staging funnel tests gave quick feedback.
- What didn't: I under-estimated coordination work with platform docs + SSO team. Need earlier syncs.
- Weird signal: a subset of users hit long-tail networking blips; may be region routing. Flag for infra.

Draft remediation checklist:
- UX: inline token-exchange example in quickstart + sample cURL and SDK snippet. (owner: me)
- Devtools: add a 'test-connection' endpoint that returns diagnostic code + help URL. (owner: infra)
- Observability: emit 'first-run-error-code' to analytics with minimal PII. (owner: me + analytics)
- Content: rewrite error copy for auth/token issues (owner: Maya)

Personal habit experiment (parallel):
- Focus slots: two 90-minute deep blocks on Mon+Thu for implementation and unblock meetings on Wed.
- Daily micro-review: 10 min at EOD to log progress and one blocker.
- Weekly demo: Friday 20-min show-and-tell (keeps pressure to ship small things).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can infra simulate region-specific network jitter to reproduce long-tail failures? (asked infra, PROJ-842)
- How to measure 'value' of quickstart beyond runs? (email capture? anonymous survey?)
- What privacy guardrails for telemetry minimal set? Loop in security.

Notes to self:
- Keep PRs small. Ship with feature flags. Revert quickly if needed.
- When in doubt: pick the smallest change that would reduce abandonment at that funnel step.
- Document every experiment briefly in the ticket (metrics, cohort, date).

Quick links (for copy-paste):
- Confluence mini-OKR template: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/PRD/mini-okrs-templates
- Infra pull: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/432

End-of-doc: last check 2025-02-04 — next formal review scheduled 2025-02-07 (demo + metrics snapshot).
